keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: a rebel state Cliopatria lacks. The page gives no boundaries or area; the Eastern Cape part of the Dutch Cape Colony's 1794 shape (the districts beyond the Gamtoos River up to the Great Fish River, 284 cells) stands for the Graaff-Reinet district, which the Dutch page says had a magistracy from 1786. Extent unverified.

ledger.note: 1795: the Graaff-Reinet district proclaims a republic against the VOC. 'In 1795, after years of oppression by the Dutch East India Company (VOC), the inhabitants proclaimed a republic.' Infobox 'Revolt Against the Dutch: 1795'; president Marthinus Prinsloo. The page gives no month.

region.text: the Graaff-Reinet district and the eastern frontier of the Cape, as it stood in 1794

ledger.note: August 1796: Britain takes Graaff-Reinet. The republic 'was from 1795 to 1796 a self-proclaimed Boer republic'; the Cape Colony 'was itself conquered by Great Britain in 1795 (and Graaff-Reinet until August 1796)'. The infobox dates the British invasion 1796, the body 1795.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundaries; the district follows the Cape's eastern frontier districts.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, written in the af-07-a batch as a counterpart of dutch-cape-colony and british-cape-colony (the Republic of Swellendam, also 1795, is not written: 'also did this' is all the Graaff-Reinet page says and no page of its own was opened). The page has no area, boundary or month for the proclamation; the extent is the Eastern Cape part of the Dutch 1794 shape (researcher's reading). Disagreement inside the page: the infobox dates the British invasion 1796, the body 1795 (the Cape Town landing; Graaff-Reinet only in August 1796). The rebellions of 1799-1803 at Graaff-Reinet are not on the page.
